No justification from the driver's side is on record: no traffic incident occurred near the route during the trip window (F15) and conditions were fair with no rain (F16); the only speed-band record (F14) shows moderate 20–29 km/h traffic, not a reason to stop 179 m short.
Because the driver cancelled on a no-show claim while never positioning his vehicle at the rider's pickup point, the $6.61 cancellation fee should not stand and must be refunded in full (F7, F4).

The driver already has one no-show dispute upheld against him in the last 90 days (F18); this second, again GPS-contradicted, no-show claim supports an additional account-review referral while remaining only an additional action, not the finding itself.

weaknesses: NS-1(iii) is met on the system record: the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 14:06:15 and stayed within 200 m for 3 min 40 s (F6), and the platform recorded arrival at 14:03:20 with 6 min 35 s elapsed before cancellation (F5) and 5 min 55 s cumulative time within 200 m (F2) — the driver will argue the no-show prerequisites were satisfied in full.
The 200 m arrival radius is only a data-layer parameter (G2), and the driver's tap position of 178 m (F6) sits just inside it; if Ryde applied a stricter radius the outcome could shift the other way.

The rider's own message (F10) only says she was "at the entrance" and does not see the driver; it does not prove she was at the exact pin location, so the driver may argue he waited at a legitimate nearby pickup spot and that the rider failed to walk to him.

The driver will rely on his own statement (F13) that he was at the pickup and walked-distance away, and on chat #1 (F9) informing the rider of his location; the case turns on preferring the GPS stationary record (F3) over that statement.

claims.assertion: The rider's no-show cancellation fee of $6.61 is valid: the platform recorded the driver's arrival at 14:03:20 (F5), the driver then tapped "I'm Here" at 14:06:15 while 178 m from the pickup point — inside the 200 m arrival radius (F6) — and the GPS track shows the driver stationary at 179 m from the pickup from 14:05:55 until the cancellation at 14:09:55 (F3), i.e. more than 3 minutes continuously waiting at the pickup point after the tap, satisfying NS-1.

The rider's charge is the standard cancellation fee of $6.61 on record (F4) with no surge multiplier (F8), so no additional or unpublished item was added and FARE-1 requires no refund of any other amount.

The driver complied with the waiting obligation: cumulative time within 200 m of the pickup before cancellation was 5 min 55 s (F2), and after the tap he remained within 200 m for 3 min 40 s (F6), which exceeds the 3-minute threshold in NS-1 (iii).

The driver gave the rider notice of his position before cancelling — chat #1 at 14:06: “I'm here, silver Toyota Altis, at the side road” (F9) — and the rider replied at 14:07 that she was at the entrance and did not see him (F10); the driver then cancelled at 14:09 after stating he had waited more than 3 minutes (F11), so the no-show was not a case of silently abandoning the rider.

Nothing in the case triggers NS-2 or NS-3: the driver did press "I'm Here" (F6), was within the pickup radius at that moment (F6), and waited more than 3 minutes thereafter (F3, F6), so the driver-side cancellation was a valid no-show cancellation rather than a no-reason cancellation.

The rider's complaint that "the driver was not at the entrance where the pin was" is answered by the system record: the driver's closest approach to the pickup point was 40 m at 14:03:50 (F1) and he then waited stationary 179 m from the pin (F3), which is inside the 200 m arrival radius NS-1 (ii) applies; a 179 m side road with fair weather and no incidents (F16, F15) is a normal pickup position, not a failure to arrive.

The chat record is complete — 3 messages, every one timestamped (F12) — so NS-1's timeline can be assessed without a G12 gap, and the driver's post-trip statement (F13) merely corroborates the GPS/timeline record rather than substituting for it.

weaknesses: The driver tapped "I'm Here" 178 m from the pin and stayed at 179 m, not at the pin itself (F6, F3); if the judge reads the rider's "I'm at the entrance, I don't see you" (F10) together with the 179 m distance as the driver not being genuinely available at the pickup point, the closeness of the call could support the rider.

The driver's second dispute in 90 days, of which 1 was upheld on a no-show (F18), gives the rider an argument for a repeated-issue narrative under RD-6-style scrutiny, although the rider's own profile shows 0 upheld disputes (F17).

The driver cancelled while the rider was actively messaging that she was at the entrance (F10, F11); the judge may view a cancellation 6 min 35 s after the platform-recorded arrival (F5) as premature once the rider had responded in chat.
The driver's own statement says he was "a short walk from the entrance" (F13) — an admission that he was not exactly at the pin, which the rider will use to argue NS-1 (ii) is not met.

points.response: Conceded on arithmetic only: the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 14:06:15, 178 m out, and stayed within 200 m for 3 min 40 s before cancelling at 14:09:55 (F6, F4), so NS-1's mechanical 200 m box was satisfied — but that same record shows he never moved to the pin (closest approach 40 m at 14:03:50, then stationary 179 m away, F1, F3), and the fee should not stand for a driver who stopped one street short of the entrance the rider named and told him she was waiting at (F10).
I do not dispute that $6.61 with no surge (F7, F8) is the published figure; the dispute is not quantum but entitlement, and NS-2 / NS-7 govern when that published fee must be refunded.

The 5 min 55 s cumulative and 3 min 40 s post-tap figures (F2, F6) do not cure the deficiency: the whole of that time was spent stationary at a point 179 m from the pickup (F3), while the rider was messaging "I'm at the entrance, I don't see you" (F10) — waiting in the wrong place is not waiting for the rider.

The driver's own notice (F9) confirms he was on "the side road," and the last system position before his cancellation is 179 m from the pin (F3); the chat therefore shows the driver knew he was not at the entrance and cancelled anyway (F9, F10, F11).

NS-1(iii) is a continuous-waiting requirement at the pickup point; the driver waited continuously 179 m away (F3), which is not the pickup point, so the driver-side cancellation is not a valid NS-1 no-show and falls into NS-2 with full refund of the $6.61.

A 200 m data-layer radius is not a licence to park 179 m away: the driver's closest approach was 40 m at 14:03:50 and he then never closed the gap (F1, F3), while the rider — the paying party who chose the Clarke Quay entrance — had no way to reach him (F10); fair weather and no incidents (F16, F15) remove any justification for that choice.

I accept the chat record is complete and timestamped (F12), and that is precisely why it defeats the driver's case: it fixes him at the side road (F9) while the rider reported being at the entrance (F10), and his post-trip statement of being "at the pickup" (F13) is contradicted by the GPS stationary position 179 m out (F3).

Withdrawn as a standalone supporting claim: I no longer rely on the timeline alone to say the no-show was complete, because the same facts show the driver was 178–179 m from the pin throughout (F6, F3); I seek the refund under NS-2 instead.
We accept this — the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 14:06:15 while 178 m from the pickup (F6), inside the arrival radius NS-1 (ii) applies, so the rider's own concession is fatal to her refund case.

The rider concedes NS-1 (iii): the driver stayed within 200 m for 3 min 40 s after the tap (F6) and cancelled 6 min 35 s after the platform-recorded arrival (F4, F5); with (i), (ii) and (iii) all satisfied, NS-1 makes the $6.61 fee valid and the correct outcome is no_action, not refund_full.

Distance from the pin is not a condition of NS-1: the clause fixes the arrival test at the driver being within the pickup radius at the tap (F6), and the driver had earlier closed to 40 m at 14:03:50 (F1) before waiting stationary 179 m from the pin (F3) — the rider cites no clause requiring the vehicle to touch the exact pin.

The rider's presence at the entrance is not enough: NS-1 requires the driver's arrival, tap and 3-minute wait (F6, F3), all of which are recorded, while the rider's own message at 14:07 (F10) shows she had not walked the short distance to the side road the driver had identified at 14:06 (F9) within the waiting time.

We do not rely on the driver's post-trip statement (F13) to establish the case; the fee stands on the system record alone — the 14:06:15 tap (F6) and the stationary GPS position 179 m from the pickup through cancellation (F3).

Reroute justification is irrelevant here: this is an NS-1 no-show case, not an RD-4 reroute claim, and the fair weather (F16) with no incidents (F15) only confirms the driver had no obstacle to waiting — which he did for 3 min 40 s (F6).

The refund request fails on the clause the rider herself invokes: NS-1 makes $6.61 the rider's liability precisely when (i)–(iii) are met, and NS-2 only applies if one of them fails — here the tap (F6) and the 3 min 40 s wait (F6) satisfy both, so no refund or fee waiver arises.

RD-6 attaches flag_account only when the case is established against the driver (refund > 0 or an RD-1 breach), and here the no-show is upheld in the driver's favour on the system record (F6, F3); the rider's own profile shows 1 dispute with 0 upheld (F17), so no account action is warranted against either party.
